inference_results.prompt:
You are the research analyst supporting a platform team deciding whether to adopt a
vector-first retrieval architecture or stay with keyword-based search for an internal
documentation portal serving roughly 40,000 pages. Leadership wants an evidence matrix, not
opinions: every claim in the final decision memo must trace to a specific source in the matrix
you produce. Your artifact will be audited line-by-line against the source pack below, and any
row citing a paper that does not exist in the pack, or attributing a finding to the wrong
paper, will invalidate the entire deliverable. The audit is automated: citation keys are
matched exactly.

SOURCE PACK (the complete evidence base — nothing outside this pack is citable):
- [BM25-baseline] Robertson & Zaragoza, "The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and
  Beyond", 2009. Establishes the classical scoring function; reports that IDF-based term
  weighting remains competitive on clean keyword-matched corpora; documents failure modes on
  vocabulary mismatch, estimating relevance drops sharply when query and document share no
  surface terms.
- [DPR-2020] Karpukhin et al., "Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering",
  EMNLP 2020. Reports top-20 retrieval accuracy 78.4 on Natural Questions versus 59.1 for
  BM25; notes dense retrieval underperforms BM25 on out-of-domain entity-heavy queries;
  training required 100k+ labeled question-passage pairs.
- [BEIR-2021] Thakur et al., "BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of
  Information Retrieval Models", 2021. Evaluates 18 retrieval systems across 18 datasets;
  finds BM25 surprisingly strong zero-shot median nDCG@10 of 41.9; most dense models trained
  on MS MARCO fail to consistently beat it out-of-domain; concludes domain shift is the
  dominant failure axis for learned retrieval.
- [Hybrid-2022] Luan et al., "Hybrid Sparse-Dense Retrieval with Learned Routing", SIGIR 2022.
  Reports a router combining BM25 and dense candidates beats both standalone systems on a
  mixed in-domain/out-of-domain workload, relative improvement 7-11% nDCG@10 over the better
  single system; routing errors concentrated on short queries under four terms.
- [ANN-cost-2021] Johnson et al., "Billion-scale Similarity Search with GPUs", IEEE TBDA
  2021. Engineering study of approximate nearest neighbor indexes: recall@1 above 0.95
  achievable at sub-10-millisecond latency for 100M vectors on a single GPU; index build and
  memory cost scale linearly with corpus size; retraining embeddings requires full reindex.
- [Rerank-2023] Nogueira et al., "Passage Reranking with Large Language Models", 2023 arc.
  Shows cross-encoder reranking of top-100 candidates lifts end accuracy substantially, at
  the cost of one LLM inference per candidate; authors recommend reranking only when first-
  stage precision is already adequate.

DECISION CONTEXT FROM STAKEHOLDERS:
- Corpus: 40k internal wiki pages, heavy jargon, product codenames, frequent rewrites.
  Query log sample: 62% of queries are four words or longer; 11% contain codenames that
  appear verbatim in fewer than five pages.
- Team capacity: two engineers for one quarter; no budget for labeling 100k pairs.
- Infrastructure: CPU-only serving today; one A100 available but shared.
- Latency budget: p95 under 150 milliseconds end-to-end for search.
- Leadership's stated worry: "every dense retrieval demo looks great until domain shift bites".

ADDITIONAL STAKEHOLDER QUESTIONS YOUR THEMES MUST ANSWER, each grounded only in the pack:
- Which architecture option does the evidence support given that our corpus is closed-domain
  but our query distribution contains entity-heavy long-tail codenames?
- What is the cheapest credible evaluation we can run in one quarter with two engineers, per
  the annotation-cost evidence?
- What infrastructure commitment does each option imply at our corpus scale, given the
  engineering numbers in the pack?
- Where would a hybrid system concentrate its failures on our query mix, and does the pack
  say those failures correlate with any segment we serve disproportionately?

SYNTHESIS DISCIPLINE. Each theme's synthesis paragraph must follow a fixed micro-structure:
claim, then the citation_keys supporting it, then the strongest counter-evidence with its
keys, then one sentence stating what the pack cannot resolve. Themes must not share
identical support sets; if two themes would cite the same sources for the same claim, merge
them or differentiate the claim. The contradictions array must contain at least two entries
and each entry must name the decision it complicates, not merely observe that sources
disagree. The confidence object must justify each value with either evidence spread (sources
pointing opposite directions), evidence volume (single engineering study versus multi-system
benchmark), or transfer distance (benchmark corpus versus internal wiki), and must never
cite common sense or intuition as justification.

SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS REQUIREMENT. The matrix must include, inside the confidence object, a
sensitivity sub-object keyed by the three decision levers the team actually controls:
annotation budget (zero versus partial versus full labeling), infrastructure commitment
(CPU-only versus dedicated GPU), and evaluation depth (offline metrics only versus online
A/B). For each lever, state in one sentence which theme's confidence would move most and in
which direction, citing keys. Do not extrapolate numeric outcomes the pack does not contain;
the sensitivity analysis is qualitative and must stay that way.

YOUR TASK: produce the evidence matrix as a single JSON object with these top-level keys:
matrix_id (string, use "vec-vs-kw-2026-q3"), sources (array), themes (array),
contradictions (array), confidence (object). The sources array must contain one entry per
source pack item, each with citation_key, venue_year, claim_count, and findings_used (array
of one-line findings actually relevant to this decision, each traceable to that source). The
themes array must contain at least: domain-shift robustness, annotation cost, latency and
infrastructure, hybrid approaches, reranking economics — each theme object listing which
citation_keys support it and a one-paragraph synthesis grounded only in those sources,
following the micro-structure above and answering the stakeholder questions it maps to. The
contradictions array must capture genuine tensions in the evidence (for example, dense
retrieval's in-domain wins versus its zero-shot losses) with the citation_keys on each side.
The confidence object must state, per theme, a confidence value between 0 and 1 and a
one-line justification per the discipline above, plus the sensitivity sub-object.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: one JSON object; first character "{" and last character "}"; no markdown, no
commentary outside the object; every citation_key must appear verbatim in the source pack
above; do not invent, merge, or abbreviate citation keys; do not attribute numbers to sources
that did not report them. Numbers you cite must match the source pack exactly. The audit
script fails the deliverable on any unknown citation key, any number not present in the pack,
and any missing top-level key.

QUALITY BAR: a skeptical staff engineer should find every cell of your matrix defensible
against the pack without accessing the original papers. Where the pack is silent — for
example on internal-wiki corpora specifically — your synthesis must say so explicitly rather
than papering over the gap.

RE-ATTEMPT (round 2). Your previous attempt did not pass.
